correctness.rationale: All positive-length minimizing graph routes reduce to direct portions and at most one junction-to-junction edge; a longer full edge can always be replaced by the strictly shorter edge. For pairs on the same long edge the transit domain consists of two triangles, combined area d_i^2/4. For pairs on distinct long edges it consists of two disjoint opposite-corner rectangles for each ordered pair, combined area d_i d_j/2. The product areas divided by L^2 yield the exact formula. The triangles and rectangles directly give the Dirichlet and independent-uniform conditional laws. Cauchy–Schwarz and positivity give both sharp fixed-total bounds, equality and nonattainment statements. A standalone independent enumeration/quadrature and 640000 random-pair simulations over eight configurations, plus conditional coordinate tests, agree within explicitly stated numerical tolerances; simulation is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The complete-edge geodesic transit load is a natural intrinsic routing measure on a canonical family of length graphs with arbitrarily many competing corridors. The result gives a complete exact edge-load spectrum (only the shortest link has nonzero through-load), sharp two-sided optimization under fixed length and fixed minimum link, and exact conditional endpoint shapes, including a simplex Dirichlet law. These features are not a relabeling of average distance or finite-vertex betweenness and support comparisons of continuous shortest-path traffic in nonuniform corridor networks. No claim about downstream network design, a universal general-graph theorem, or independent priority is required.
